newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran MP says U.S. embargo slows foreign investment.
newsitem.headline: Iran MP says U.S. embargo slows foreign investment.

text.p: U.S. sanctions against Iran have slowed foreign investments in the Iranian oil industry, a member of parliament said in remarks published on Tuesday.

"Despite widespread arrangements by the (oil) ministry, foreign contractors are not much interested in engaging in petroleum projects in Iran," Mohsen Yahyavi, a senior member of the parliament's oil commission, was quoted as saying by the daily Iran News.

In a rare admission by an Iranian political figure, Yahyavi blamed the U.S. trade and investment ban imposed by Washington in June 1995 against Tehran for the lack of interest of investors to engage in 10 large oil and gas projects offered by Iran.
The United States tightened the sanctions last year to include non-U.S. firms that invest $40 million or more in Iran's oil and gas industries.

Yahyavi, who originally made the remarks to the daily Abrar, said the lack of interest was due to the projects being offered as "buy-back" schemes, in which the investors are paid back from the projects' production.
Iran said in early December it would award within about two months two of the 10 projects which would require investments totalling $4 billion to $5 billion.
Iran's open-door oil policy was launched with the signing in 1995 of a $600 million deal with France's Total SA to develop the Sirri A and E oil and gas fields.
Central Bank Governor Mohsen Nourbakhsh, quoted by the daily Jomhuri Eslami, said Iran had received foreign investments worth $1.2 billion since September 1995. He did not give comparative figures.
